61: Effective date of the benefit reduction under 5313(a)(1): the court held the reduction starts on the sixty-first day after conviction (July 19, 2006), not after sentencing. This is the earlier of the two candidate dates and so falls under the first outcome label, but it helps the VA.
Thus, according to its ordinary meaning, a 'conviction' occurs when the accused is found—or pleads—guilty; the convicted felon's 'sentencing' is separate and distinct from the determination of guilt.
166: Effective date of benefits: whether an effective date earlier than May 30, 2002 (the reopened-claim filing date) is available for the veteran's psychiatric disability award.
The earliest effective date for an award based on a claim to reopen [based on new and material evidence] is the date of that claim, not the date of the original claim.
863: Effective date for the secondary back condition: court affirmed an April 27, 2007 effective date rather than the earlier February 22, 2006 date the veteran sought.
The Veterans Court did not err in awarding an April 27, 2007, effective date for Ms. Manzanares's secondary service connection claim.
1327: Effective date for PTSD disability compensation; court held claim remained pending from 1995 referral so earlier effective date applies

We reverse the Veterans Court's decision denying Mr. Sucic's claim for an earlier effective date for his PTSD disability compensation and remand for further findings and determinations on the effective date for his PTSD claim.
1381: Effective dates: challenge to the September 12, 1988 effective date for non-service-connected pension benefits; court declined to review because effective date is a question of fact.
Because Mr. Clay only challenges the effective date of his pension benefits, he merely raises an issue of fact.
1787: Effective date of increased compensation for depression: the court affirmed the May 4, 2010 effective date (the later date) rather than the March 2010 claim date sought by the veteran.
We therefore see no reversible error in the Veterans Court's affirmance of a separate effective date for Mr. Oldfield's depression as a secondary disability.
1938: Effective date for special monthly pension for aid and attendance: the court held that the implicitly raised 1993 SMP claim remained pending until 2005, so the effective-date question must be reconsidered on remand.
Mr. Batson's implicitly raised SMP claim remained pending from 1993 until SMP was granted in 2005.
2956: Effective date for service-connected PTSD; court affirmed denial of an effective date earlier than June 5, 2006.
we see no error in the Board's interpretation of § 3.156(c)(1) or in the Veterans Court's affirmance of the Board's interpretation.
3288: Effective date of disability benefits: whether benefits should begin at discharge in 1984 rather than the 2007 claim-filing date, given lack of notice of eligibility

Those provisions leave no room for an effective date before the claim-filing date just because Mr. Titone was not told that he had the option to file a claim for such benefits when he left active service.
4136: Effective date for the MDD service-connection award; the court held Sellers is not entitled to the earlier March 1996 effective date based on his formal claim.
Accordingly, Mr. Sellers is not entitled to the earlier effective date he requests.
4743: Effective dates: whether an earlier effective date than February 6, 2013 is warranted for service-connected coronary artery disease; the Federal Circuit did not reach the merits and dismissed for lack of jurisdiction.
Because Mr. Curtis’s appeal raises only such issues, we dismiss for lack of jurisdiction.
5312: Effective dates for diabetes, secondary erectile dysfunction, and coronary artery disease under the liberalizing herbicide presumptions; Board correctly denied earlier effective dates than February 25, 2010 and August 31, 2010.
The Board made no error in denying Mr. Davis earlier effective dates.
5939: Effective date of Mrs. Ruel's DIC award: whether the 1984 claim remained pending so the effective date is July 6, 1984 rather than October 20, 2009
the correct effective date of Mrs. Ruel's DIC claim is July 6, 1984, and we direct the VA to dispense her benefits accordingly.
6089: Whether Lacoste is entitled to an effective date reaching back to his 1972 application for his mood-disorder benefits; the court affirmed the denial of the earlier effective date.
we affirm the Veterans Court's decision.
6578: Effective date for service-connected PTSD; court affirmed denial of an effective date earlier than June 5, 2006, under § 3.156(c)(3) and § 5110.

We therefore once again affirm the decision of the Veterans Court that affirmed the decision of the Board denying Mr. Kisor entitlement under § 3.156(c)(1) to an effective date earlier than June 5, 2006, for his PTSD.
6673: Effective date for service connection for depression: court affirmed denial of an effective date earlier than March 4, 2008.
The Veterans Court also did not err in affirming the Board's decision denying Mr. Brunette an effective date earlier than March 4, 2008, for service connection for depression.
6885: Effective date of the PTSD benefits award: October 7, 2002 (date of request to reopen) rather than June 7, 1994 (date of original claim).
Thus, as the Board held, the proper effective date was the date of the request for reopening, not the date of the initial claim.
7149: Effective date for the 60 percent disability rating; court affirmed April 2, 2007 date of diagnostic testing rather than earlier date from physician's order.
No medical evidence in the record supports his entitlement to an effective date earlier than April 2, 2007.
7263: Effective date for service-connected skin condition benefits; the court declined review of the Board's finding that the 1985 forms were not a claim, treating it as a non-reviewable factual determination.
To the extent Mr. Harris seeks review of this finding, it is a factual determination that cannot be disturbed by this court.
7279: Effective date for service-connected back benefits: the veteran is entitled to an earlier effective date following the CUE holding.
Mr. Cousin is entitled to an earlier effective date for his benefits.
7452: Effective date for the 20% rating for residuals of a right knee meniscal tear: the court held the Veterans Court did not err in finding no entitlement to an effective date earlier than November 8, 2014, because no increase in disability was ascertainable in the year before the claim.

Thus, we hold that the Veterans Court did not err in construing 38 U.S.C. §5110(b)(3) when it found that Mr. Chatman is not entitled to an effective date earlier than November 8, 2014 for a 20% rating for residuals of a medial meniscus tear.
7652: Effective date for PTSD disability benefits: the court held the Government equitably estopped from asserting 38 U.S.C. 5110(a)(1) against Taylor's claim, so an earlier effective date (1971 discharge-based) is available.
We reverse the Veterans Court and hold the Government equitably estopped from asserting 38 U.S.C. § 5110(a)(1) against Mr. Taylor's claim.
7846: Effective date for sleep apnea benefits: whether Sampson's 2000 PTSD claim constituted an informal claim for sleep apnea, so as to support an August 31, 2000 effective date rather than March 31, 2013.

To the extent his appeal contends that the Veterans Court did not apply the correct legal requirements for determining whether Mr. Sampson had filed an informal claim in 2000 for sleep apnea, we detect no legal error.
8148: Whether the timeliness of Board action on a pending SMC appeal is measured from the claim's effective date; court declined to adopt a broad rule using the effective date
we decline to adopt a broad rule stating the timeliness for Board action on pending appeals is assessed from a claim's effective date.
8266: Effective date of the award: veteran entitled to May 22, 2011 rather than May 22, 2012
the correct effective date for Mr. Ortiz's benefits is May 22, 2011, rather than May 22, 2012.
8431: Effective date of disability compensation: the court affirmed that the effective date is the August 25, 2006 application date, rejecting the claimed 1976 effective date based on an alleged attempted application.
We affirm the Veterans Court's decision that the effective date for Mr. Rivera's compensation award is the 2006 application date.
8449: Effective date of PTSD benefits: award upheld as effective August 5, 2009 (date of the 2009 reopening request), not the 1999 initial claim date.
As a result, he received benefits retroactive to August 5, 2009, the date he filed that request to reopen.
8548: Effective date of increased 30% disability rating for pseudofolliculitis barbae with disfigurement; court affirmed the April 26, 2011 effective date and rejected the earlier August 2000 date based on medical records not being an informal claim.
Mr. Bennett appealed the Regional Office's decision to the Board, which affirmed.
8686: Effective date of the 100 percent PTSD rating: court upheld October 26, 2015 as the effective date rather than the earlier May 30, 2014 date sought by the veteran.

Accordingly, we uphold the decision of the Veterans Court that Mr. Gudinas is entitled to an effective date of October 26, 2015, for his 100 percent disability rating for PTSD, not an effective date of May 30, 2014.
8797: Effective date: the court affirmed that the effective date could not be pushed back to the 1979 reopening request, leaving the May 2, 1992 effective date in place.
Therefore, we affirm the Veterans Court's law-of-the-case conclusion.
9112: En banc court unanimously held equitable tolling is not available to give Arellano an effective date earlier than the date his benefits application was received; the court was equally divided on the reasons and on tolling of 38 U.S.C. 5110(b)(1) in other circumstances.
a unanimous court holds that equitable tolling is not available to afford Mr. Arellano an effective date earlier than the date his application for benefits was received.
9603: Equitable estoppel is barred by OPM v. Richmond and cannot override the claim-filing effective-date limit of 38 U.S.C. 5110, so no earlier effective date follows from estoppel.
We therefore hold that, under Richmond, equitable estoppel is not available to override the claim-filing effective-date limits of § 5110.
9606: Remedy: Taylor is entitled to the effective date he would have had absent the unconstitutional denial of access, which may be as early as September 7, 1971.

A veteran in Mr. Taylor's position is entitled, under ordinary remedial principles, to receive benefits for service-connected disabilities from the effective date that the veteran would have had in the absence of the government's challenged conduct.
9809: Effective dates: whether Bryce is entitled to an earlier effective date for TDIU than May 12, 2006, based on the pending 1976 informal claim.
Accordingly, absent some exception to finality (which Mr. Bryce did not supply), there was no basis for assigning an earlier effective date for his TDIU.
9874: Effective date for recommencement of disability benefits after active service: court upheld the February 1, 2008 effective date under the one-year look-back rule
Because the VA reasonably filled a statutory gap when promulgating 38 C.F.R. § 3.654(b)(2), we must defer to that regulation.
9968: Effective date for service-connected PTSD: whether the 2008 claim served as an informal claim for PTSD, which would have set an earlier effective date than November 2016; the court held it did not.

We therefore agree with the Veterans Court that "the Board was not required to anticipate an informal claim for PTSD that was not reasonably raised by the record or reasonably encompassed within the 2008 claim for breathing problems and fatigue."
10237: Effective date for right knee and right ankle service connection; the court did not reach the merits, as jurisdiction was lacking
Because Mr. Chapman disputes factual findings and the application of laws to the facts of his case, we lack jurisdiction over his appeal.
10304: Effective dates for disability benefits: the court affirmed the denial of earlier effective dates (cervical DDD September 19, 2005; reopened headaches claim March 31, 2006; lumbar DDD February 17, 2009).
We affirm the Veterans Court’s determination that Mr. Sanders was not entitled to earlier effective dates.
10319: Effective date: court affirmed denial of an effective date earlier than April 4, 2014, because the December 2012 decision became final and no appeal remained pending.
As a result, the December 6, 2012 RO decision became final.
10368: Effective date for secondary right-knee disability; court held the April 11, 2006 date stands rather than February 23, 2005.
Because § 3.156(b) has no bearing on the effective date of Mr. Jordan's secondary right-knee disability, the Board did not err in not discussing it.
11014: Effective date for the service-connected depressive disorder; the court affirmed the denial of an earlier effective date than May 8, 2013, finding the Veterans Court applied a correct prejudicial-error standard.
Accordingly, we see no error in the legal standard the Veterans Court used for assessing prejudicial error.
11532: Effective date for service-connected lung cancer; whether an earlier effective date based on the April 2005 informal claim applies given the presumption that VA sent Form 21-526 after the informal claim.
In sum, the Veterans Court did not err in presuming that the VA sent VA Form 21-526 with the April 23, 2005 letter.
11739: Effective date: whether Williams is entitled to an effective date earlier than June 4, 2009, based on the finality of the July 1978 rating decision. The court affirmed the denial of an earlier effective date.
we affirm the Veterans Court's decision denying Mr. Williams's appeal for an earlier effective date for his service-connected disability benefits.
12275: Effective date for service connection of OSA, diabetes mellitus and hypertension; the April 1, 2008 later date was affirmed.
the Veterans Court held the Board did not err when it denied an earlier effective date for Mr. Dietrich's claims.
12390: Effective date: whether the earlier effective date claim for PTSD remained pending or was finally denied by the 2015 Board decision; court held it was finally adjudicated, so no earlier effective date.
Mr. Moore does not identify a pending claim in need of adjudication but, instead, attempts to alter the results of the Board's final determination.
13886: Effective date for service-connected left hip degenerative joint disease; whether 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(c) reconsideration based on service department records permits an earlier effective date than July 17, 2001

We conclude that because Mr. Harris's 2001 claim for service-connected disability was granted in March of 2016 based upon his post-2001 examinations, his claim fell under the provisions of 38 C.F.R. § 3.156(a) for "new and material" evidence, not the provisions of § 3.156(c) for "service department records."
14319: Effective date for service-connected headaches: the implicit denial in 1991 finally adjudicated the claim, so the effective date is no earlier than March 6, 2013.
We see no legal error in this analysis or the Board's findings or the Veterans Court's affirmance.
14363: Whether equitable estoppel can override the § 5110 claim-filing effective-date limits, so that the effective date is later than the 2010 diagnosis-based date sought by the veteran.
equitable estoppel is not available to override the claim-filing effective-date limits of § 5110.
14887: Effective date: the Board's grant of an April 1990 effective date and denial of an earlier 1987 effective date were affirmed because the new regulation was properly applied prospectively.
Because the new regulation was invoked in 2008, the Board's application of the new regulation in its 2022 Decision was prospective and proper.
15134: Effective date: the court affirmed denial of an effective date of October 1991 for the psychiatric disorder, leaving the later August 2003 or March 1995 date in place.
Neither Bond nor Beraud support Mrs. Deal's position.
15303: Effective date for right leg radiculopathy: the veteran sought a 2008 effective date based on her 2009 notice of disagreement; the court held that the 2009 notice did not place radiculopathy into appellate status, so the March 2019 effective date stands absent a timely notice of disagreement to the 2019 decision.

The Veterans Court therefore correctly decided that if Ms. De Hart wished to challenge the regional office's 2019 decision with regard to her right leg radiculopathy claim, she needed to file a timely notice of disagreement with respect to that decision.
